title: Wild number for spanning trees in complete and complete bipartite graphs
summary: Given an edge-colored graph, the wild number measures how close the graph is to having a spanning tree in every color. We investigate this parameter for complete graphs and complete bipartite graphs, with particular emphasis on minimum proper colorings and equitable $2$-colorings. For complete graphs, we determine the full range of wild numbers attainable by equitable $2$-colorings and show that, although every value in this range occurs, the expected wild number of a uniformly random equitable $2$-coloring tends to $0$ as the order of the graph grows.
